entities.projectDescription: The ACABA REDD+ Project is located in the General Community Council of the Baudó River and its Tributaries (ACABA) on the Pacific coast of the department of Chocó. The Project contains very humid tropical forest with transition to tropical pluvial forest, and has unique habitat conditions for both flora and fauna. It is considered an invaluable region at the national and international level and is classified as one of the of the most biodiverse hotspots on Earth, characterized by the presence of endemic species. Significant and exponential deforestation has occurred in the region over time, which according to the IDEAM forest monitoring report for the 2010-2017 period was 10,559 ha. This scenario is the caused by a lack of territorial planning, which in turn results in processes associated with wood extraction, the expansion of the agricultural frontier, the establishment of crops for illicit use, unplanned infrastructure, the construction of new road accesses, and itinerant open-pit mining. The project uses a standalone approach and an annual average of 208,556 tCO2e are expected to be reduced with a total reduction of 6,465,226 tCO2e over the project’s lifetime of thirty years. With the implementation of the REDD+ project, the community will achieve the reduction of emissions resulting from deforestation and forest degradation, and thereby environmental and social benefits will be generated. Additionally, economic resources will be available to be invested in the creation of productive opportunities aimed at improving the living conditions of the inhabitants, in alignment with the ACABA ethno-development plan. The Project is eligible under the VCS Program and uses the VM0009, v3 Methodology. The project will have a AUDD activity type baseline scenario, using Colombia’s national Forest Reference Emissions Levels (FREL). The project will generate GHG emission reductions by reducing unplanned deforestation, covering activities within the scope of the VCS Program.

entities.projectDescription: Proyecto REDD+ para mitigar el cambio climático, proteger la rica biodiversidad y generar fuentes de ingresos para las comunidades pobres, a través de la gobernanza forestal, el desarrollo de capacidades y las actividades productivas que evitarán la tala selectiva de bosques nativos, evitando la degradación y la deforestación. Ubicado en Tumaco, costa suroeste del Pacífico de Colombia. Desarrollado por BIOREDD+/USAID

entities.projectName: AFFORESTATION OF DEGRADED GRASSLANDS IN VICHADA, COLOMBIA
entities.projectDescription: The grouped project aim is to recover degraded grasslands in Vichada, Colombia, through the establishment of timber plantations. The first instance consists of the afforestation of 30,605 ha of low-fertility grasslands that have been degraded by livestock in the municipalities of Puerto Carreño and La Primavera, it includes the planting of Eucalyptus (Eucalyptus pellita) and Acacia (Acacia mangium) as timber species. Through afforestation activities to recover degraded lands, the project aims to promote connectivity between ecosystems. In addition, this project is expected to provide more than 200 full-time employment opportunities (with equal access to women and men) in a zone historically affected by poverty. Furthermore, the increase in the forest cover and sequestration of carbon in living biomass will contribute to the reduction of GHG emissions by acting as sink that sequesters an average of 139,489 tCO2e per year.

entities.projectDescription: The ASATIQ Vaupés Maloca REDD+ Project is located within the area of the Association of Traditional Indigenous Authorities of Querarí (ASATIQ), which is part of the Great Eastern Indigenous Reservation of Vaupés in jurisdiction of the municipality of Mitú, in the department of Vaupés, Colombia. ASATIQ’s territory is located in the Colombian Amazon biome. The objective of the ASATIQ Vaupés Maloca REDD+ Project is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions coming mainly from deforestation and degradation of the Amazon Forest. Potential activities to reduce deforestation include forest protection and monitoring, the intensification and improvement of agricultural productivity in local communities, planting of fruit and timber trees (including those used for firewood), planting of other species used as construction materials, the creation of jobs as an alternative source of income (for example, in forest monitoring) and the improvement of health and education conditions of the communities in order to offer non-extractive work options. At the same time, actions in the medium and long terms have been defined to support the territory’s self-governance principles, as well as to promote the development of local traditional practices and ancestral education. The proposals made are framed aligned with the general action lines of the ASATIQ Life Plan. On the other hand, between 40% and 60% of recent IDEAM deforestation early warning bulletins come from the Amazon, and the department of Vaupés appears in the first five ranks of alert. Under these circumstances, the without-project scenario presents an unplanned use of forest resources with extractive logging activities and the expansion of the agricultural frontier through subsistence crops and itinerant mining, which are being developed progressively putting at risk the ecosystem balance of the forests and the cultural traditions of the communities. The duration of the project is proposed from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2047.

entities.proponents: Association of Traditional Indigenous Authorities of Querarí (ASATIQ)

entities.projectDescription: The ASATRIZY Vaupés Maloca REDD+ Project proposed to be implemented in the Great Eastern Reservation of Vaupés is in the Reduced Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD+) category. Development of the REDD+ project is based on the VM0009 Methodology, v3 of the VCS. This methodology is applicable to this project and is being used for other REDD+ projects in the region. It has also been used by Wildlife Works, having two types of areas of application.  The first, corresponding to the Project Area (PA) and the second to the Project Accounting Area (PAA). The PAA is the area with forest cover, where the project would implement activities to prevent deforestation and whose results would be used to calculate carbon credits. According to the territory conditions, this is a standalone project that respects ASATRIZY’s autonomy. In the without-project scenario, the forest ecosystems in the department of Vaupés and in particular those in the territory of ASATRIZY are located in life zones of tropical humid forest. This area has been recognized as one of the most biodiverse in the country and the whole continent, being characterized by its endemic species. The forest monitoring carried out by the Colombian Government and coordinated by IDEAM has shown a national annual deforestation average between 177,764 ha and 219,552 ha for the 2016-2017 period, with the Amazon biome representing 70% of the total deforestation. In addition, between 40% and 60% of recent IDEAM deforestation early warning bulletins come from the Amazon, and the department of Vaupés appears in the first five ranks of alert. According to this scenario and based on data obtained from the Amazonian Scientific Research Institute (SINCHI) and through field visits carried out by WWC, it was possible to identify the unplanned use of forestry resources as the main driver of deforestation in the project area, consisting of “slash-and-burn” activities in the jungle to expand the chagras.
